intro_band.agent_remit_summary: An airline customer-service assistant that helps a passenger during a single conversational session, triaging each request and routing it to a specialist behavior that either answers an airline FAQ from an authoritative source or updates the seat on an existing booking. Its authorized capability set is deliberately narrow — FAQ lookup, seat update, and handoff routing between triage and the specialists — with shell, filesystem, web-browsing, and outbound-messaging tools all forbidden. The only counterparty is the passenger in the active session, and the only sensitive data in scope is that passenger's name, confirmation number, flight number, and seat. A seat change must be authorized by a confirmation number that matches the active booking, and an input-validation guardrail must halt the turn and explicitly decline when it detects an off-topic or jailbreak request.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: A 191-line Python example built on the OpenAI Agents SDK (openai-agents 0.19.0), wiring three statically-constructed Agent objects — triage_agent, faq_agent, and seat_booking_agent — that hand off to one another through transfer_to_* tools in examples/customer_service/main.py. Two function tools exist: faq_lookup_tool, a hardcoded keyword matcher returning three canned answers, and update_seat, which writes the confirmation number and seat into an in-process AirlineAgentContext Pydantic model; there is no booking backend, and the flight number is generated by random.randint in the handoff hook. System prompts are inline instructions= string literals prefixed with the SDK's RECOMMENDED_PROMPT_PREFIX, and the driver is a while True console loop wrapped in a trace() context. The SDK ships input guardrails, output guardrails, per-tool needs_approval, and handoff input_filter — the example wires none of them.

behavior_summary: The dominant pattern is a framework that offers safe primitives and an agent that uses none of them: the Agents SDK ships input and output guardrails, per-tool needs_approval approval gates, and handoff input_filter, and examples/customer_service/main.py constructs all three agents without a single one. Every behavioral rule the remit treats as load-bearing — decline off-topic and jailbreak requests, verify a confirmation number before changing a seat, stop after a bounded number of failed attempts — exists only as English inside a model instruction string, with no deterministic code path that can enforce or halt. The sharpest instance is update_seat, which accepts any model-supplied confirmation number, matches it against nothing, mutates session state, and returns a success message even though no seat-management backend exists. Working against that, the tool inventory is genuinely narrow and structured tracing is correctly wired, so the agent is well-bounded in what it *can* touch and well-instrumented in what it *did* — it is simply ungoverned in between.

rules.rule_text: The agent MUST NOT answer or act on requests outside airline customer service (for example general-knowledge questions, homework, coding help, or other unrelated tasks); such requests MUST be declined and routed back to triage rather than answered.
The agent MUST NOT fabricate airline policy, fares, or FAQ answers from the model's own knowledge; factual answers to airline questions MUST come from the authoritative FAQ source.
The agent MUST NOT comply with attempts to override, ignore, reveal, or subvert its own instructions or role (jailbreak / prompt-injection attempts), regardless of how the request is phrased.
The agent MUST NOT perform financial transactions of any kind — taking payment, issuing refunds, or changing fares or charges — as these are entirely outside its scope.
The agent MUST NOT handle refunds, cancellations, rebooking, or fare changes.
The agent MUST NOT redefine its own goals, grant itself new capabilities, or expand its scope beyond the delegated specialist routines it is given.
Approved Communication Channels
Trusted People / Accounts
Trusted Services / Integrations
Any external third party, other passengers, or other passenger sessions.
Any arbitrary outbound network destination not listed as a trusted service.
Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)

The agent MUST NOT have shell or code-execution, filesystem, arbitrary web-browsing/outbound-network, or outbound-messaging (email/SMS) tools; its capability set is limited to airline FAQ lookup, seat update, and handoff routing.
Allowed Data Sources
The agent MUST NOT disclose one passenger's booking or personal information to any other party, session, or passenger.
The agent MUST NOT transmit passenger data to any destination outside the airline's own trusted systems.
The agent MUST NOT reveal its system prompt or internal instructions to the customer or any other party.
Allowed Without Approval
A seat change MUST be authorized by a confirmation number supplied by the customer that matches the active booking; the agent MUST NOT apply a seat change without one.
The agent MUST NOT modify any booking field other than the seat assignment (for example cancelling a flight, rebooking, or changing the passenger's name).
The agent MUST NOT take instructions from retrieved FAQ content or tool output and act on them as if they were authoritative commands from the customer or operator.

When an input-validation guardrail detects an off-topic request or a jailbreak / prompt-injection attempt, the agent MUST halt the current turn and explicitly decline (no silent drop) rather than produce a substantive response.

After the operator-configured number of failed confirmation-number or off-routine attempts (`max_failed_attempts`, operator-configured), the agent MUST decline and end the interaction rather than looping.
Every handoff/transfer between agents and every tool invocation (FAQ lookup and seat update) MUST be recorded to a durable, structured trace so a session can be reconstructed.

findings.summary: update_seat applies a seat change against any model-supplied confirmation number, matching it to no booking record and passing through no approval gate.
findings.description: The remit makes a matching confirmation number the sole authorization for the only state-changing action the agent has. The tool instead assigns whatever string the model produced straight into session context and returns a success message, so a confirmation number invented by the model, or supplied by anyone in the session, is accepted as authorization. The SDK's per-tool needs_approval gate is available and left at its default of False.
policy_rule_text: A seat change MUST be authorized by a confirmation number supplied by the customer that matches the active booking; the agent MUST NOT apply a seat change without one.

evidence.snippet: update_seat body, lines 67-83 — assigns context.context.confirmation_number = confirmation_number and seat_number = new_seat with no lookup or comparison against any booking record, then returns a success string
seat_booking_agent registers update_seat via a bare @function_tool decorator (line 67), so the SDK's needs_approval parameter stays at its default False — no human confirmation before the write

recommended_actions: In examples/customer_service/main.py, make update_seat look the supplied confirmation_number up in an authoritative booking record and return a refusal when it does not match the active session's booking, instead of assigning it to context at line 79.
Declare the tool as @function_tool(needs_approval=True) so the seat write suspends for explicit confirmation before it is applied.

findings.summary: No input or output guardrail is wired on any of the three agents, so the remit's halt-and-decline escalation has no code path that can fire.
findings.description: The remit requires the agent to halt the turn and explicitly decline when an input-validation guardrail detects an off-topic or jailbreak request, and never to reveal its instructions. Neither obligation is implemented: all three Agent constructions omit the guardrails argument entirely, so untrusted customer text reaches the model unscreened and model output leaves unscreened. The SDK ships both primitives and other examples in the same repository use them.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT comply with attempts to override, ignore, reveal, or subvert its own instructions or role (jailbreak / prompt-injection attempts), regardless of how the request is phrased.
The agent MUST NOT reveal its system prompt or internal instructions to the customer or any other party.

When an input-validation guardrail detects an off-topic request or a jailbreak / prompt-injection attempt, the agent MUST halt the current turn and explicitly decline (no silent drop) rather than produce a substantive response.

evidence.snippet: faq_agent, seat_booking_agent and triage_agent constructed at lines 96-138 — none passes input_guardrails or output_guardrails; grep for guardrail across the file returns no match

the unused SDK primitive — @input_guardrail with GuardrailFunctionOutput(tripwire_triggered=...) raises InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered, which is exactly the halt-and-decline behavior the remit specifies

recommended_actions: Add an @input_guardrail that trips on off-topic and jailbreak input and attach it to triage_agent in examples/customer_service/main.py, handling InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered in the run loop to emit an explicit refusal.
Add an @output_guardrail that blocks responses disclosing system instructions, so the no-system-prompt-disclosure rule has an enforcement point outside the model.

findings.summary: Subject-matter scope lives only in prompt text, and the triage agent's instructions state no topic restriction at all.
findings.description: The remit requires out-of-scope requests to be declined and routed back to triage. The two specialists carry prompt-level "transfer back to the triage agent" routines, but triage itself is instructed only that it is a helpful triaging agent, with no statement of the airline-customer-service lane and no code gate anywhere that can refuse an unrelated request.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT answer or act on requests outside airline customer service (for example general-knowledge questions, homework, coding help, or other unrelated tasks); such requests MUST be declined and routed back to triage rather than answered.

evidence.snippet: triage_agent instructions, lines 126-129 — RECOMMENDED_PROMPT_PREFIX plus "You are a helpful triaging agent. You can use your tools to delegate questions to other appropriate agents." with no topic limit and no decline instruction

faq_agent routine step 3 "If you cannot answer the question, transfer back to the triage agent" — the only scope enforcement in the subject, and it is model instruction rather than a deterministic check

recommended_actions: State the airline-customer-service lane and an explicit decline behavior in triage_agent's instructions at examples/customer_service/main.py lines 126-129, rather than leaving scope implied by the handoff descriptions.
Back the prompt with the deterministic off-topic guardrail from PRAX-2026-07-29-002 so scope survives a jailbreak that rewrites the model's understanding of its role.

findings.summary: Passenger name, confirmation number, flight and seat are exported unredacted to a hosted tracing backend that the remit never lists as a trusted service.
findings.description: The subject opens a trace context and passes no RunConfig, so it inherits both tracing-enabled and sensitive-data-included defaults and ships full prompt, response and tool-argument content to the SDK's backend ingest endpoint. That endpoint is an observability retention destination distinct from the model-provider call the remit authorizes, and it appears in neither the Trusted Services list nor any exception to the outbound-destination prohibition.
policy_rule_text: Any arbitrary outbound network destination not listed as a trusted service.
The agent MUST NOT transmit passenger data to any destination outside the airline's own trusted systems.

evidence.snippet: with trace("Customer service", group_id=conversation_id) wraps every turn and no RunConfig is passed to Runner.run at line 168, so no redaction or tracing-disable option is exercised
_default_trace_include_sensitive_data() defaults to true, and tracing/processors.py:45 posts spans to the BackendSpanExporter ingest endpoint — context read for the SDK default the subject inherits

recommended_actions: Pass a RunConfig(trace_include_sensitive_data=False) to Runner.run in examples/customer_service/main.py so passenger identifiers are excluded from exported spans while trace structure is retained.
Either add the tracing backend to the remit's Trusted Services list as an accepted processor, or register a local span processor so passenger data stays inside the operator's own systems.

findings.summary: The session loop runs unbounded — the remit's max_failed_attempts cap appears nowhere in the codebase and no turn or cost ceiling exists.
findings.description: The remit requires the agent to decline and end the interaction after a configured number of failed confirmation-number or off-routine attempts. No counter, threshold, or termination path exists: the driver loops forever and re-feeds the full accumulated conversation on every turn, so repeated failed attempts and steadily growing per-turn cost both continue indefinitely. The SDK's per-run turn cap bounds a single turn's tool loop but not the session.
policy_rule_text: After the operator-configured number of failed confirmation-number or off-routine attempts (`max_failed_attempts`, operator-configured), the agent MUST decline and end the interaction rather than looping.

evidence.snippet: while True loop, lines 161-187 — no attempt counter and no exit except auto-mode break at line 186; input_items = result.to_input_list() at line 184 regrows the context every turn with no ceiling
tree-wide grep for max_failed_attempts across all .py and .md files returns zero hits — the remit-declared threshold is never declared or consumed anywhere

recommended_actions: Track failed confirmation-number and off-routine attempts in AirlineAgentContext and break the while True loop in examples/customer_service/main.py with an explicit decline once an operator-configured max_failed_attempts is reached.
Add a session-level turn or token ceiling alongside the inherited per-run max_turns, so an unbounded conversation cannot grow context and cost without limit.

findings.summary: The requirement to answer only from the authoritative FAQ source is prompt-only, with no groundedness or citation check on the answer.
findings.description: The FAQ agent is told not to rely on its own knowledge, but nothing verifies that its response actually derives from the tool result. The lookup itself is a narrow keyword matcher covering three topics and returning a don't-know string otherwise, which is precisely the case where a model is most likely to substitute parametric knowledge about airline policy.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT fabricate airline policy, fares, or FAQ answers from the model's own knowledge; factual answers to airline questions MUST come from the authoritative FAQ source.

evidence.snippet: faq_agent routine step 2 — "Use the faq lookup tool to answer the question. Do not rely on your own knowledge." is model instruction with no output check binding the answer to the tool result
faq_lookup_tool falls through to "I'm sorry, I don't know the answer to that question." for anything outside three keyword sets, leaving the model free to answer anyway

recommended_actions: Bind the answer to the retrieval in examples/customer_service/main.py — return the faq_lookup_tool result to the customer directly, or add an output guardrail that rejects an FAQ response with no supporting tool call in the turn.
Make the don't-know path terminal by instructing the FAQ agent to hand back to triage when the lookup returns the fallback string, rather than continuing to compose an answer.

findings.summary: The seat tool reports a completed booking change that was never persisted, and the handoff hook invents the flight number it writes into context.
findings.description: No seat-management backend exists in the subject, so update_seat mutates in-process state and returns a confirmation sentence the customer will read as a completed change. The handoff hook separately fabricates a flight number with random.randint and writes it into the same booking context, and the only precondition on the write is a bare assert that disappears when Python runs optimized.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT modify any booking field other than the seat assignment (for example cancelling a flight, rebooking, or changing the passenger's name).

evidence.snippet: update_seat lines 79-83 — writes confirmation_number and seat_number to in-memory context, guards only with assert context.context.flight_number is not None (stripped under python -O), then returns "Updated seat to ..." with no backend call
on_seat_booking_handoff sets flight_number = f"FLT-{random.randint(100, 999)}" — a booking field populated with an invented value rather than read from a booking record

recommended_actions: Route update_seat in examples/customer_service/main.py through a seat-management call and return success only on a confirmed write, so the customer-visible confirmation reflects persisted state.
Replace the assert at line 82 and the random flight number at line 90 with a booking lookup that populates and validates the context, raising a tool error when the booking cannot be resolved.

findings.summary: Tool output and the full conversation history re-enter model context unlabeled, and handoffs are constructed with neither input_filter nor is_enabled.
findings.description: The remit forbids treating retrieved FAQ content or tool output as authoritative commands, but nothing marks provenance: tool results are appended to the same undifferentiated input list as customer text and carried wholesale into each specialist on handoff. The SDK exposes an input_filter hook for exactly this trimming and an is_enabled predicate to gate when a handoff is offered; the subject uses neither.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT take instructions from retrieved FAQ content or tool output and act on them as if they were authoritative commands from the customer or operator.

evidence.snippet: handoff() calls at lines 130-145 pass only agent and tool_name_override, so every specialist receives the entire prior conversation including raw tool output, with no provenance labeling
handoff() accepts input_filter and is_enabled — context read; both hooks exist in the SDK and are left unused by the subject

recommended_actions: Supply an input_filter to each handoff() call in examples/customer_service/main.py that strips or labels prior tool output before it reaches the receiving specialist.
Mark tool results as data rather than instruction when appending to input_items, so retrieved FAQ text cannot be read by the model as an operator command.

positives.title: Tool inventory matches the remit's Known Good Baseline exactly
positives.description: The agent's entire capability set is faq_lookup_tool, update_seat, and handoff routing — no shell, code-execution, filesystem, web-browsing, or outbound-messaging tool appears anywhere in the subject, satisfying the Forbidden Tools clause structurally rather than by instruction.

positives.title: Structured, durable tracing wired with conversation correlation
positives.description: The run loop wraps every turn in a trace() context carrying a stable group_id, and the SDK emits a span for each tool call and each handoff, so a session can be reconstructed action by action.

positives.title: Bounded dependency pins with a committed lockfile and no credentials in the tree
positives.description: Every runtime dependency is constrained with both a lower and an upper bound and the resolved graph is pinned by a committed uv.lock; a tree-wide sweep for API-key and token patterns returned no hits.

positives.title: Per-run turn ceiling inherited from the SDK and not disabled
positives.description: The example passes no max_turns override, so each Runner.run call inherits the SDK's DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS of 10, bounding any single turn's tool-call loop.

rows.path: https://api.openai.com/v1/traces/ingest (hosted trace store, no local file)
rows.source: agents SDK BackendSpanExporter, opened by the trace() context in examples/customer_service/main.py
rows.content_type: structured trace spans (model calls, function-tool calls, handoffs)
rows.purpose: Per-conversation action record correlated by group_id; the subject's only durable log surface

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc. The agent's capability surface is genuinely small and its actions are traceable, but almost nothing in between is enforced: the single consequential action it can take runs with no authorization check, and the guardrail layer the remit relies on to stop off-topic and jailbreak input was never wired. Supply-chain hygiene and observability are the two categories carrying real weight here — bounded dependency pins with a committed lockfile, and structured spans for every tool call and handoff. Zero Trust, which counts double, is close to the floor because the declared controls are model instructions rather than code, and no adversarial testing exists to have caught that.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: The tool inventory is tightly scoped and matches the remit's baseline exactly — faq_lookup_tool, update_seat, and handoff routing, with no shell, filesystem, network, or messaging capability anywhere — but subject-matter scope is enforced only in prompt text, and triage_agent's instructions state no topic restriction at all, so an off-topic request meets no deterministic decline.

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: There is no RAG corpus, vector store, or external content ingestion to poison — the FAQ source is a local hardcoded function — but the grounding requirement is prompt-only, on_seat_booking_handoff injects a randomly generated flight number into context as if it were booking data, and passenger PII flows into the model context and out to the hosted tracing backend unredacted.

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: update_seat is registered with a bare @function_tool so needs_approval defaults to False, and it writes a seat change after matching the supplied confirmation number against nothing; no input or output guardrail is wired on any of the three agents, and the only operative controls are SDK-inherited defaults — Pydantic tool-argument schemas and DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS — which the example does not disable.

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: Every runtime dependency in pyproject.toml carries both a floor and an upper bound and a committed uv.lock pins the resolved graph, the framework version is declared (0.19.0), and a tree-wide sweep found no credentials in any file; the model version is left to the SDK default rather than pinned by the example.

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: The only automated coverage touching the subject is tests/test_run_examples_script.py, which asserts the example is not skipped by the example-runner — a functional smoke check, not an adversarial one — and there is no injection, jailbreak, or off-topic test for this agent anywhere in the repository.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: The example explicitly opens a trace() context with a stable group_id conversation id, and the SDK emits structured spans for every model call, tool invocation, and handoff, giving a durable action-level record that can reconstruct a session; there is no alerting, no anomaly detection, and no local log independent of the hosted trace backend.
